To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the text representation schemes are classified into two main categories, namely, feature based and non-feature based text representation schemes; 2) feature based schemes can be further divided into three subcategories, namely, term frequency based, document frequency based and statistical schemes; 3) the non-feature based schemes are further divided into four sub-categories, namely, vector space model, Latent Semantic Analysis, Latent Semantic Indexing and Latent Semantic Analysis with Singular Value Decomposition; and
, the text representation scheme and classifier used to classify text document to the predefined classes are dependent on each other.

the classification accuracy of the classifiers depends on the representation of the text documents, the features used to represent the text documents and the learning algorithms used for classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: 1) How to represent the document for the classification?

the following: 1) A brief review of text representation schemes and classification algorithms, 2) Comparison of various classifiers based on the criteria used for classification and classification time complexities and 3) A comparative study of the classification accuracies of different text classifiers.
the representation and classification of text documents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single text representation or classification method that is best for all applications.

, there is no one best method that is suitable for all text documents, but the selection of the best method is based on the type of the document, the type of classification, the number of classes and other parameters.
the classification accuracy depends on the text representation scheme and the classifier used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the classification accuracy of text documents depends on the text representation and the classifier used.
the text representation scheme is an important factor that influences the performance of the text classification algorithms.
, the text classification is a very challenging task and it is not possible to find the best text representation scheme for all text classification problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the text documents can be classified using various text representation schemes, classifiers/learning algorithms.
the existing methods can be used for classification of text documents based on the nature of text documents.
the classification accuracy is highly dependent on the representation schemes and classifiers used for classification.
